report:

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Left medial knee pain after tripping and striking left knee on a box at work.  History of RA. 
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.  

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES: 
Marked marrow edema in the lateral tibial plateau. Alignment is anatomic.  No aggressive osseous lesions.  

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst. 

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Radial oblique tear of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus with mild extrusion. 6 x 3 mm parameniscal cyst at the posterior horn, body junction. 
Medial compartment cartilage: Diffuse high-grade cartilage loss, weightbearing portion of the femoral condyle. 8 x 5 mm full-thickness cartilage defect posterior weightbearing portion of the femoral condyle. High grade partial thickness cartilage loss of the tibial plateau. 

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.  
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low-grade cartilage fraying spanning the lateral compartment. 

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT: 
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Mild heterogeneity of the patellar cartilage.     

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.  
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.  

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal. 
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.  
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal. 

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear. 
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear. 
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.  
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad.  No lateral patellar tilt or translation.  No patella alta.  Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 13 mm. 

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy.  Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact. 

SOFT TISSUES:
Edema identified in the medial subcutaneous fat. 
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle. 

IMPRESSION:
1.	Intense marrow edema in the medial tibial plateau. Findings may reflect contusion or severe osseous stress response/developing stress fracture.
2.	Radial oblique tear of the medial meniscus with mild extrusion.
3.	High-grade medial compartment chondrosis.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: [PROFESSION]. Diffuse right knee pain after knee to knee collision(s). 
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
There is a moderate, diffuse bone contusion involving the most anterior aspect of the medial femoral condyle and a mild, small contusion at the most anterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle. There is a moderate focal bone contusion at the lateral aspect of the patella. No acute fracture on MRI. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
There is a moderate joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: There is mild blunting/fraying of the inner margin of the medial meniscus without tear.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: There is partial thickness, in part delaminating cartilage fissuring (grade 3 chondral fissuring) at the central weightbearing aspect of the lateral femoral condyle (se 8, img 8 to 12). Very small marginal osteophytes.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: There is a chronic, 15 x 15 mm full-thickness cartilage defect (grade 4 chondral defect) at the groove of the femoral trochlea extending into the lateral aspect of the trochlea with subchondral cystic change. There is partial thickness cartilage fissuring (grade 2 chondral fissuring) at the medial and lateral patellar facets. 

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal. There is a mild contusion/sprain of the joint capsule of the proximal tibiofibular joint.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: There is bony fragmentation of the tibial tubercle consistent with Osgood Schlatter Mild tendinosis and fraying and of the proximal and distal patellar tendon without tear . 
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 18 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:. 
1. Moderate, diffuse bone contusion involving the most anterior aspect of the medial femoral condyle and a mild, small contusion at the most anterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle. Additional moderate focal bone contusion at the lateral aspect of the patella.
2. Moderate joint effusion. 
3. Moderate chronic patellofemoral chondrosis and mild lateral compartment chondrosis. 
4. Mild contusion/sprain of the joint capsule of the proximal tibiofibular joint.
5. Osgood Schlatter with chronic tendinosis and fraying of both the proximal and distal patellar tendon without tendon tear. 
6. No meniscal or ligament tears.

Small suprapatellar effusion, a cluster of variably sized ossific loose bodies is appreciated posteromedially, the largest on measuring just over 1 cm across.

The medial meniscus appears intact.  
There is incomplete, chronic looking loss of lateral meniscal tissue throughout the corresponding posterior half, together with diffuse full-thickness chondral loss affecting the lateral tibial plateau.
No displaced meniscal fragments are present. 

Focal grade 3 chondral loss noted at the medial retropatellar facets, relatively mild age-related thinning of medial weightbearing hyaline cartilage.
There are nonetheless medial and lateral femorotibial marginal osteophytes.
Intact cruciate and collateral ligaments, popliteus musculotendinous unit, distal iliotibial band and the patellar tendon.
Chronic looking calcific, quiescent distal insertional quadriceps tendinosis.
No fracture or marrow infiltration.
Grossly unremarkable imaged extra-articular soft tissues.
